resources.string: How the airways clear trapped particles
A simplified view of the lining in conducting airways, not the air sacs. Shapes, distances and playback time are not to scale.
When inhaled particles settle on the airway lining, the sticky surface mucus can trap them.
Goblet cells release mucins, the large molecules that help form a mucus gel above the cilia.
Cilia beat within the fluid layer beneath the mucus. Their coordinated strokes push the gel in the same direction.
The moving mucus carries trapped particles from the conducting airways toward the throat.
Mucus can be swallowed into the esophagus. The esophagus is separate from the airway.
